definitions.explanation: The Buddhist concept of the continuous cycle of birth, death, and rebirth that all living beings undergo until they attain enlightenment.

examples.japanese: {輪廻|りんね}から{解脱|げだつ}する。
examples.english: To be liberated from the cycle of rebirth.

examples.japanese: {仏教|ぶっきょう}では{輪廻|りんね}の{教|おし}えが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: In Buddhism, the teaching of reincarnation is important.

examples.japanese: {魂|たましい}は{輪廻|りんね}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}しながら、やがて{悟|さと}りに{至|いた}ると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that the soul goes through repeated cycles of rebirth and eventually reaches enlightenment.

notes:
A key concept in Buddhism and Hinduism. In Japanese Buddhism, {輪廻|りんね} describes the cycle of suffering through repeated births and deaths in the six realms ({六道|ろくどう}). Attaining {悟|さと}り (enlightenment) allows one to escape this cycle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {輪廻転生|りんねてんしょう} (transmigration of souls, metempsychosis)
- {輪廻|りんね}から{逃|のが}れる (to escape the cycle of rebirth)
- {輪廻|りんね}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す (to go through cycles of rebirth)

Also read as りんえ in some classical Buddhist texts, though りんね is the standard modern reading. Frequently appears in literature, anime, and games as a theme.
